Use Tier 2 architectural deepening: add learned relative-position biases to SASRec’s causal self-attention, focusing on model_design and training_evaluation. The latest trial achieved macro HR@10 of 0.485 versus the baseline’s 0.505, with the largest losses in Movies_and_TV and Electronics. These results justify testing a stronger sequence inductive bias, although they do not establish the cause of the plateau. The hypothesis is that absolute positional embeddings alone make interaction distance and recency unnecessarily difficult to learn from sparse histories.

Add a trainable, per-attention-head bias indexed by the distance between each query and its preceding keys, using exact buckets for nearby interactions and logarithmic buckets for longer distances. Apply this bias to attention logits before softmax while retaining causal masking and excluding padded keys, so future interactions remain inaccessible. Train these parameters jointly with the existing network and retain the current sampler, ranking loss, optimizer, dimensions, and training schedule to isolate this architectural change. Keep the supplied splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four categories, and DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Select exactly one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10 on fixed candidate banks with 200 users and 99 unique negatives at evaluation seed 42, and report the four-category macro-average. Update the predictor writer and checkpoint configuration to reconstruct the same relative-position architecture and use identical history processing during validation and host inference, with every score produced by that category’s single trained model.
